results.topic: Why local AI evaluation loops matter more than model size
results.draft:
When I built a local RAG chatbot for a client, the model size felt like a checkbox—until the system started failing under real-world load. The real issue wasn’t the number of parameters; it was the lack of a robust evaluation loop.  

Without continuous feedback from user interactions, we couldn’t detect when the system was hallucinating or misaligning with business goals. Model size matters, but only if it’s paired with a system that can measure, adapt, and improve.  

Local AI tools give you control over this loop. You can iterate faster, debug more precisely, and ensure your model behaves as intended—not just in theory.  

For ML engineers and founders, the lesson is clear: build the evaluation loop first. It’s the difference between a model that works and one that actually *helps*.

results.topic: The expensive mistake of building features nobody asked for
results.draft:
Last week, I spent a week building a fancy RAG chatbot for content drafting — all the bells and whistles, local tooling, and custom workflows. By the end, it was impressive. But the moment I showed it to a real user, they said, “This is great, but I just need a simple prompt template.”

The mistake? I built for the future, not the present. I assumed the need, not the demand.  

Early-stage founders: Always ask, “Who is this for?” before building. The most expensive mistake isn’t bad code — it’s building features nobody asked for.  

Focus on the problem, not the solution. The rest will follow.

results.topic: Incentive design beats slogans in product and market decisions
results.draft:
In my experience with AI product design, slogans often feel like a quick fix—until the numbers don’t match. A recent project showed that while a catchy slogan drove initial engagement, it failed to sustain user behavior.  

The real leverage came from aligning incentives. When we introduced a tiered reward system for consistent usage, retention jumped by 37%.  

Incentive design isn’t just about rewards—it’s about shaping the *cost* of inaction.  

For product leaders and economists, the lesson is clear: slogans may grab attention, but incentives drive outcomes.

results.topic: Treat writing quality like CI: fail tests for generic AI phrasing
results.draft:
In a recent AI project, I saw code churn spike from vague prompts like "write a compelling article on AI trends." The output was generic, repetitive, and failed to meet stakeholder needs.  

Like CI, writing quality needs automated checks. I built a test suite to flag phrases like "AI is transforming everything" or "the future is here." These are red flags—no value, no specificity.  

When I ran the tests, the AI draft failed 80% of the time. It wasn’t the model’s fault—it was the prompt.  

Treat writing like code. Fail fast on generic phrasing. Build tests for clarity, depth, and relevance.  

#AI #Writing #Engineering #CI #ContentQuality #RAG #LLM
